name: X-linked spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and radiological diagnostic criteria for X-linked SEMD

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate short stature with short trunk and limb shortening
Radiographic evidence of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia including vertebral flattening and metaphyseal irregularities
Identification of pathogenic variants in the TRAPPC2 gene
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males in multiple generations
Correlation of clinical phenotype with characteristic radiological abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features, radiological findings, and confirmation by genetic testing of TRAPPC2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other skeletal dysplasias.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Disproportionate short stature with short trunk
searchTerms: short height with disproportionately short torso
disproportionate body length with short trunk

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metaphyseal irregularities and epiphyseal dysplasia on imaging
searchTerms: abnormal metaphysis and epiphysis on X-ray
skeletal dysplasia with bone shape changes

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness and limited range of motion
Gait abnormalities due to limb shortening
searchTerms: gait issues due to limb shortening
abnormal walk caused by short legs or arms

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications secondary to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: breathing issues due to chest wall deformities
respiratory problems from rib cage abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to spinal cord compression
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure causing neurological signs
weakness or numbness from spinal tumor

imaging: Platyspondyly with flattened vertebral bodies on spine X-rays
Irregular metaphyses and epiphyseal dysplasia on long bone radiographs
Possible hip dysplasia on pelvic imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TRAPPC2 gene (X-linked inheritance)
other: Family history consistent with X-linked pattern
Disproportionate short stature with short trunk

distinguishingFeatures: Severe short stature with prominent facial features

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits suggesting spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage deformity
Rapidly worsening joint deformities or early-onset severe osteoarthritis
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
